chunks: There was a token for you in the two armies which clashed (in the battle of Badr), one fighting for God, the other of unbelievers who saw with their own eyes the faithful to be two times as many as they, for God reinforces with His help whomsoever He will. In this is a lesson for those who have eyes.

key_terms.أُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ: those who have eyes / people of insight
key_terms.رَأْيَ الْعَيْنِ: with the eye of sight / with their own eyes

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the two armies in Surah Al-Imran verse 13?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al-Imran (3:123) explicitly references the Battle of Badr, where the Muslims, despite being outnumbered two-to-one, achieved a decisive victory through divine assistance. In Shia scholarship, this event is often viewed as a manifestation of the spiritual authority (Wilayah) of the Ahl al-Bayt, illustrating that true strength lies in faith and divine support rather than material numbers. It serves as a timeless lesson for believers to maintain steadfastness and insight (ulil-absar) in the face of overwhelming opposition.
